FAQ

What is MacBook Clamshell Mode?

Clamshell Mode — also called Closed Display Mode — is when a MacBook runs with the lid closed while connected to power and an external monitor, with an external keyboard and mouse or Bluetooth input. The built-in display stays off while macOS continues the desktop session on external displays. AppLocale rewrites how you describe that closed-lid MacBook story on your App Store product page — not the system behavior itself.

How is Clamshell Mode listing copy different from Sidecar?

Clamshell Mode is MacBook lid closed on external monitor — 合盖模式, 闭盖外接显示. Sidecar is iPad as Mac second display — 随航, 副屏. MacBook closed-display desktop and iPad extended desktop use different gallery art, buyer intent, and zh-Hans vocabulary. See our Sidecar listing guide when iPad-as-display is your lead — not this clamshell page.

How is Clamshell Mode different from Stage Manager and Universal Control?

Stage Manager markets multitasking windowing on each device's own screen — 台前调度. Universal Control markets one keyboard and mouse across Mac and iPad — 通用控制. Clamshell Mode markets MacBook with lid shut running desktop on external displays — 合盖模式. Listing copy should name the surface each frame actually shows.
